slides.title: 4 syntax tricks that *cut your code in half*
slides.subtitle: Old way vs new way. Swipe and save.

slides.heading: 1. *Inline* declarations
slides.left:
DATA lv_count TYPE i.
lv_count = lines( lt_orders ).

slides.heading: 2. *Table* expressions
slides.left:
READ TABLE lt_mara INTO ls_mara
  WITH KEY matnr = lv_matnr.
IF sy-subrc = 0.
  lv_mtart = ls_mara-mtart.
ENDIF.
slides.right:
lv_mtart = VALUE #(
  lt_mara[ matnr = lv_matnr ]-mtart
  OPTIONAL ).

slides.heading: 3. Fill a table with *VALUE*
slides.left:
ls_item-matnr = 'MAT-01'.
ls_item-menge = 10.
APPEND ls_item TO lt_items.

slides.heading: 4. *String* templates
slides.left:
CONCATENATE 'Order' lv_vbeln
  'saved' INTO lv_msg
  SEPARATED BY space.

slides.heading: sy-subrc: what it means after each statement
items: 4 after READ TABLE / SELECT - Row not found
8 after READ TABLE ... BINARY SEARCH - Not found, past the end of the table
1, 2, 3... after CALL FUNCTION - The EXCEPTIONS you numbered
Check it immediately - The next statement overwrites it

posts.caption:
sy-subrc ko ignore karna = production me dump 💥

Har ABAP developer ke liye ek quick cheat sheet. Rule simple hai: statement ke turant baad check karo, kyunki next statement isko overwrite kar deta hai.

Save karo aur apne fresher dost ko tag karo 👇

slides.title: This one line can read your *ENTIRE* table
slides.voiceover: सुनो, एक मिनट रुको। ये एक लाइन... आपकी पूरी टेबल पढ़ सकती है। और ज़्यादातर फ्रेशर्स ये गलती करते हैं।
slides.spoken: Suno, ek minute ruko. Ye ek line aapki poori table padh sakti hai. Aur zyada-tar freshers ye galti karte hain.
slides.subtitle: The FOR ALL ENTRIES trap

slides.heading: Looks *innocent*, right?
slides.code:
SELECT vbeln, posnr, matnr
  FROM vbap
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
  WHERE vbeln = @lt_orders-vbeln
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_items).
slides.voiceover: ये सेलेक्ट देखो। बिल्कुल नॉर्मल लग रहा है ना? ऑर्डर्स की टेबल से, हम वीबैप के आइटम्स पढ़ रहे हैं।
slides.spoken: Ye SELECT dekho. Bilkul normal lag raha hai na? Orders ki table se hum VBAP ke items padh rahe hain.

slides.heading: If lt_orders is *empty*...
slides.body:
the WHERE clause is ignored.

SAP reads every row of VBAP. Millions of rows. Timeout. Angry user.
slides.highlight: Empty driver table = no filter at all
slides.voiceover: लेकिन ट्विस्ट ये है। अगर ऑर्डर्स वाली टेबल खाली हुई, तो व्हेयर कंडीशन पूरी तरह इग्नोर हो जाती है। और सैप, पूरी वीबैप टेबल उठा लेता है। लाखों रोज़। सीधा टाइमआउट।
slides.spoken: Lekin twist ye hai. Agar orders wali table khaali hui, to WHERE condition poori tarah ignore ho jaati hai. Aur SAP poori VBAP table utha leta hai. Laakhon rows. Seedha timeout.

slides.heading: The fix: *one IF*
slides.code:
IF lt_orders IS NOT INITIAL.
  SELECT vbeln, posnr, matnr
    FROM vbap
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
    WHERE vbeln = @lt_orders-vbeln
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_items).
ENDIF.
slides.note: Bonus: remove duplicates from lt_orders first.
slides.voiceover: फिक्स? बस एक इफ। सेलेक्ट से पहले चेक करो, कि टेबल इनिशियल नहीं है। और हो सके तो, डुप्लिकेट्स भी पहले हटा दो।
slides.spoken: Fix? Bas ek IF. SELECT se pehle check karo ki table initial nahi hai. Aur ho sake to duplicates bhi pehle hata do.

slides.title: Follow for *daily ABAP tips*
slides.body: This one comes up in interviews all the time.
slides.voiceover: ये सवाल इंटरव्यू में भी पक्का आता है। तो पोस्ट सेव कर लो, और ऐसी ही टिप्स के लिए, फॉलो करो अबैप कोड वॉल्ट।
slides.spoken: Ye sawaal interview mein bhi pakka aata hai. To post save kar lo, aur aisi hi tips ke liye follow karo ABAP Code Vault.

posts.caption:
One missing IF, and the report read the entire VBAP table.

With FOR ALL ENTRIES, an empty driver table means the WHERE condition is ignored and every row is selected. Always check IS NOT INITIAL first, and remove duplicates from the driver table.

This is a classic interview question, so save it.

160 more interview questions with answers: ABAP Interview Pack, link in bio.

slides.heading: *STANDARD* table
slides.body:
Access by index or linear search on key. Duplicates allowed.

Use for small tables and ALV output.
slides.highlight: Read cost grows with table size

slides.heading: *SORTED* table
slides.body:
Always kept sorted by its key. Reads use binary search automatically.

Use when you read by a partial key or need data in order.

slides.heading: *HASHED* table
slides.body:
Access only by the full unique key. Constant read time, no index access.

Use for big lookup tables inside loops.

slides.heading: Declare *all three*
slides.code:
DATA lt_std TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF mara
  WITH EMPTY KEY.
DATA lt_srt TYPE SORTED TABLE OF mara
  WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY mtart.
DATA lt_hsh TYPE HASHED TABLE OF mara
  WITH UNIQUE KEY matnr.

posts.caption:
Interviewer: "What's the difference between standard, sorted and hashed tables?"

Learn to answer it in 30 seconds:
- Standard: small tables, ALV output, index access
- Sorted: reads by partial key, data kept in order
- Hashed: lookups by full unique key, constant speed
